entry.idea: n8n lets technical teams connect their apps and build AI agents that do work automatically, like onboarding a new employee or turning plain language into API calls.
entry.lesson: Serve both non-coders and developers in the same tool, let people self-host it, and an active open-source community can carry a lot of the growth.
entry.name: n8n

growth.reason: It raised a $180M round at a $2.5B valuation and reached unicorn status, a big jump backed by real numbers.

market.reason: Workflow automation and AI agents can be used by IT, security, sales and operations teams in almost any company worldwide.

tech.reason: It combines a visual builder with real code and can be self-hosted, which is solid engineering but automation tools like this exist elsewhere too.

entry.twist: Unlike drag-and-drop-only automation tools, n8n lets you write real JavaScript or Python inside any step, and you can run it on your own servers instead of only in someone else's cloud.
entry.who_pays: Businesses such as Vodafone and Huel pay to automate security, HR and operations workflows at scale; Deutsche Telekom is both an investor and a partner.
entry.why_now: Companies want to plug AI agents into the tools they already use, without giving up control of their data or being locked into one vendor's cloud.
